source.label: thm:alpha_larger_than_0
source.quote: Let $\alpha >0$, the number of arms be $k = 2$ and $m^*_1>m^*_2$. Let $\Pi_0$ be a prior where $\mathbb{P}_{\Pi_0}(M_2 > M_1 ) > 0$. For any error threshold $\epsilon > 0$, there is a deterministic mapping $f(\Pi)$ such that for all $t\geq 0$: 1. Sampling from $Q_t= f(\Pi_t)$ chooses arm $2$ with a constant probability. 2. $D_{\alpha} (\Pi_t,Q_t) < \epsilon$. Therefore sampling from $Q_t$ for $T/10$ time-steps and using any policy for the remaining time-steps will cause linear frequentist regret.
